title: Fire Protection — Aft Cargo Compartment — Inspection of the Ceiling Rail and Sampling Tube Before Port Relocation
abstract: One-time survey of the aft hold ceiling rail attachment condition and of the smoke sampling tube, taken as a screening step before the shielded inlet relocation kit is ordered.

sections.planning_reason: The relocation bulletin reuses the existing ceiling rail holes to carry the shielded inlet, which is heavier than the open port it replaces. Isolated cases of hole elongation have been reported where cargo restraint loads have been taken through the rail, and one aircraft showed corrosion at a tube clamp position. The rate is expected to be low and most aircraft should pass without further action, but a survey before the kit is ordered costs little and avoids an aircraft being opened for a modification it cannot receive.
sections.description: This bulletin is a survey only. It records the hole condition at four rail positions, the corrosion state at the clamp positions and the internal condition of the sampling tube, and gives the acceptance limits for the relocation. No parts are changed and the aircraft configuration is unaffected. The reply form is returned so that the fleet rate can be established.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Remove the aft hold ceiling lining panels at the sampling positions. Do a detailed visual inspection of the ceiling rail at the four positions given in the bulletin and measure each hole with the supplied gauge. Do a detailed visual inspection for corrosion at the two clamp positions. Disconnect the sampling tube at the regulator and do a flow check to confirm the tube is clear, then reconnect. Record the results on the reply form and return it. Refit the lining panels. If any hole exceeds the limit, contact the manufacturer before ordering the relocation kit.
sections.effectivity_note: Applies to MERIDIAN-42 and MERIDIAN-46 aircraft between MSN M00022 and M00290 that have not embodied MOD-168024. Aircraft delivered with the post modification standard do not require this survey. An operator that prefers to order the relocation kit without surveying first may do so at its own risk.
sections.material_note: No kit. The hole gauge is supplied on loan against the reply form and is returned after use. Consumables are limited to the lining panel fasteners, which are locally available.

type_data.compliance_time: Before ordering the kit for Service Bulletin MRD-26-1012, at the operator's convenience.

title: Fire Protection — Aft Cargo Compartment — Inspection of the Ceiling Rail and Sampling Tube Before Port Relocation

issue.reason: Measured fleet elongation rate published and the survey restated as a firm prerequisite of the relocation bulletin rather than an optional screening step.

abstract: One-time inspection of the aft hold ceiling rail attachment condition and of the smoke sampling tube, establishing whether an aircraft can accept the shielded inlet relocation without rail repair. Eleven of the first one hundred and forty aircraft inspected could not.

sections.planning_reason: The relocation bulletin reuses the existing ceiling rail holes to carry the shielded inlet, which is heavier than the open port it replaces. One hundred and forty aircraft have now been inspected under this Service Bulletin and eleven of them, one in thirteen, carried hole elongation outside the acceptance limit at one or more of the four rail positions; a further three showed corrosion at a tube clamp position. That is well above the rate assumed when this Service Bulletin was first issued as a screening step, and it means an operator that orders the relocation kit without inspecting first has a real chance of opening an aircraft that cannot receive it. The rate has been reported to continued airworthiness for the fleet record.
sections.description: This bulletin is an inspection only. It records the hole condition at four rail positions, the corrosion state at the clamp positions and the internal condition of the sampling tube, and gives the acceptance limits for the relocation. No parts are changed and the aircraft configuration is unaffected. It is a prerequisite of the relocation bulletin and not a convenience: an aircraft outside the limit needs rail repair scheduled before the relocation kit is of any use to it.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Remove the aft hold ceiling lining panels at the sampling positions. Do a detailed visual inspection of the ceiling rail at the four positions given in the bulletin and measure each hole with the supplied gauge. Do a detailed visual inspection for corrosion at the two clamp positions. Disconnect the sampling tube at the regulator and do a flow check to confirm the tube is clear, then reconnect. Record the results on the reply form and return it. Refit the lining panels. If any hole exceeds the limit, contact the manufacturer before ordering the relocation kit.
sections.effectivity_note: Applies to MERIDIAN-42 and MERIDIAN-46 aircraft between MSN M00022 and M00290 that have not embodied MOD-168024. Aircraft delivered with the post modification standard do not require this inspection. This Service Bulletin must be accomplished and its reply form returned before Service Bulletin MRD-26-1012 is started on the same aircraft; the wording at the first issue that allowed an operator to skip it is withdrawn.
sections.material_note: No kit. The hole gauge is supplied on loan against the reply form and is returned after use. Consumables are limited to the lining panel fasteners, which are locally available.

type_data.compliance_time: Before the accomplishment of Service Bulletin MRD-26-1012 on the same aircraft, and before the relocation kit is ordered for it.

revision_history.reason: Fleet elongation rate published and the inspection restated as a prerequisite
